original_question: For the Lie superalgebra osp(1|2), can one complete the final identification over the two independent parameters c0 + d0^2 and d0^2 and thereby derive a genuine super-triangle sum rule, expressed with the supertriangle Delta_S and parity-independent 6-j^S symbols, that plays the same role for osp(1|2) that the ordinary triangle sum rule plays for su(2) and su_q(2)?
target_in_paper: Section 13, “Ultimate identification process over (c0 + d0^2), d0^2,” together with the quasi-final Δ^S-sum rule of Section 12 and the restatement in the Conclusion: the unresolved step is to complete the final identification over the two independent osp(1|2) parameters so as to obtain a veritable osp(1|2) triangle sum rule. ([academia.edu](https://www.academia.edu/77591116/Concept_of_a_veritable_osp_1_2_super_triangle_sum_rule_with_6_j_S_symbols_from_intrinsic_operator_techniques_an_open_problem))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s actual open problem: the missing final identification over the two independent parameters c0 + d0^2 and d0^2; the goal of deriving a genuine osp(1|2) super-triangle sum rule; the central role of the supertriangle Δ^S rather than the ordinary su(2)-type triangle factor; and the use of parity-independent 6-j^S symbols. It also correctly frames the question as the osp(1|2) analogue of the ordinary su(2) and su_q(2) triangle sum rules. ([academia.edu](https://www.academia.edu/77591116/Concept_of_a_veritable_osp_1_2_super_triangle_sum_rule_with_6_j_S_symbols_from_intrinsic_operator_techniques_an_open_problem))
missing_details: The paper works in the intrinsic-operator setting of iterated tensor operators S_κ(c0,d0), not for arbitrary osp(1|2) recoupling data in isolation. These operators are defined from S_{1/2} by the three relations [S_{1/2}×S_{1/2}]^0 = c0·1^0, [S_{1/2}×S_{1/2}]^{1/2} = d0·√2·S_{1/2}, and [S_{1/2}×S_κ]^{κ+1/2} = S_{κ+1/2}, with c0,d0 assumed real. ([academia.edu](https://www.academia.edu/77591116/Concept_of_a_veritable_osp_1_2_super_triangle_sum_rule_with_6_j_S_symbols_from_intrinsic_operator_techniques_an_open_problem))

To be stand-alone, the question should say that the desired identity is not the whole derivation from scratch but the completion of the quasi-final Δ^S-sum rule already obtained in Section 12, especially equation (12.5), after using the unified closure relation (11.5) and recoupling of the triple product [[S^a×S^b]^c×S^d]^e. ([academia.edu](https://www.academia.edu/77591116/Concept_of_a_veritable_osp_1_2_super_triangle_sum_rule_with_6_j_S_symbols_from_intrinsic_operator_techniques_an_open_problem))

The admissible variables are osp(1|2) spin labels a,b,c,d,e and summation index f that may be integral or half-integral; triangle perimeters may also be integral or half-integral; and the internal sums run in steps of 1/2. Those parity conventions are part of the problem’s scope. ([academia.edu](https://www.academia.edu/77591116/Concept_of_a_veritable_osp_1_2_super_triangle_sum_rule_with_6_j_S_symbols_from_intrinsic_operator_techniques_an_open_problem))

The unresolved identification is specifically over homogeneous polynomials in the binomial basis {(c0 + d0^2)^{Ω-m}(d0^2)^m}_{m=0}^Ω, coming from products of the closure polynomials P^π and from products of γ-coefficients. Section 13 makes this explicit through the polynomials R_Ω and the degree formulas for Ω and Ω_f. ([academia.edu](https://www.academia.edu/77591116/Concept_of_a_veritable_osp_1_2_super_triangle_sum_rule_with_6_j_S_symbols_from_intrinsic_operator_techniques_an_open_problem))

The paper’s hidden obstruction is the unknown expansion coefficients x_m^π(λ,κ) in P^π(λ,κ) = (d0)^{τ_π} Σ_{m=0}^{[π]} x_m^π(λ,κ)(c0 + d0^2)^{[π]-m}(d0^2)^m. Conjecture 1 says these coefficients are integers, and this conjectural polynomial structure is part of the intended formulation. ([academia.edu](https://www.academia.edu/77591116/Concept_of_a_veritable_osp_1_2_super_triangle_sum_rule_with_6_j_S_symbols_from_intrinsic_operator_techniques_an_open_problem))

The paper does not merely ask for some osp(1|2) triangle identity; it seeks a unified veritable Δ^S-sum rule. Section 13 says one expects only two τ-parity types a priori and hopes for a unified form; otherwise one would face an “infinity” of Δ^S-sum rules. ([academia.edu](https://www.academia.edu/77591116/Concept_of_a_veritable_osp_1_2_super_triangle_sum_rule_with_6_j_S_symbols_from_intrinsic_operator_techniques_an_open_problem))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should exclude simply reusing Zeng’s older relation with ordinary triangles: Appendix C explicitly says that, even after rewriting it with parity-independent 6-j^S symbols, it remains far from the ‘veritable’ osp(1|2) triangle sum rule sought in this paper. ([academia.edu](https://www.academia.edu/77591116/Concept_of_a_veritable_osp_1_2_super_triangle_sum_rule_with_6_j_S_symbols_from_intrinsic_operator_techniques_an_open_problem))
refined_question: For the intrinsic family of iterated osp(1|2) tensor operators S_κ(c0,d0), with c0,d0 ∈ R defined by [S_{1/2}×S_{1/2}]^0 = c0·1^0, [S_{1/2}×S_{1/2}]^{1/2} = d0·√2·S_{1/2}, and [S_{1/2}×S_κ]^{κ+1/2} = S_{κ+1/2}, can one complete the unresolved “ultimate identification process” left after the quasi-final relation (12.5), namely identify, for all admissible integral or half-integral spins a,b,c,d,e and summation index f, the homogeneous polynomials arising from products of the closure polynomials P^π in the binomial basis {(c0 + d0^2)^{Ω-m}(d0^2)^m}_{m=0}^Ω — where P^π(λ,κ) = (d0)^{τ_π} Σ_{m=0}^{[π]} x_m^π(λ,κ)(c0 + d0^2)^{[π]-m}(d0^2)^m and the x_m^π are conjecturally integral — so as to derive a genuine unified osp(1|2) triangle sum rule written in terms of the supertriangle Δ^S and parity-independent 6-j^S symbols, rather than the earlier ordinary-triangle-type relation analyzed in Appendix C? ([academia.edu](https://www.academia.edu/77591116/Concept_of_a_veritable_osp_1_2_super_triangle_sum_rule_with_6_j_S_symbols_from_intrinsic_operator_techniques_an_open_problem))
justification: This is the nearest paper-faithful sharpening of your draft because Section 12 already reaches only a preliminary Δ^S-sum rule, equation (12.5), while Section 13 states that the real unresolved task is the “ultimate identification process” over the two independent parameters (c0 + d0^2) and d0^2 through a countable family of binomial identifications. The Conclusion then repeats that precisely this missing identification should yield the osp(1|2) triangle sum rule, and Appendix C explains why Zeng’s earlier relation is not the veritable rule sought here. Conjecture 1 matters because the whole identification problem is organized around the expansion coefficients x_m^π of the P^π polynomials. ([academia.edu](https://www.academia.edu/77591116/Concept_of_a_veritable_osp_1_2_super_triangle_sum_rule_with_6_j_S_symbols_from_intrinsic_operator_techniques_an_open_problem))
